observations.observation: Netlist publicly announced that it and Micron had agreed to a five-year patent license and mutual release of pending proceedings between them. The stated fee schedule was $30 million per quarter from Q4 2026 through Q3 2031, totaling $600 million.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The release is the issuer’s announcement; the fees were prospective, not reported as received. It does not enumerate the proceedings or establish that docket-level dismissals had already been entered.

observations.observation: Before the settlement announcement, the USITC had instituted a DRAM investigation, 337-TA-1523, involving Micron; the Commission said it had not decided the merits. Netlist later announced a separate HBM-related complaint seeking an investigation and remedies against Micron and downstream customers.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The USITC’s statement concerns the instituted DRAM investigation; the separate HBM complaint was described by Netlist as a request for investigation, not a Commission finding or merits determination.

observations.observation: A September 2 Federal Circuit opinion affirmed the PTAB’s conclusion that all challenged claims of Netlist’s ’339 patent were unpatentable as obvious in the Micron appeal.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This was an adverse ruling in a specific patent matter; it does not establish the status or merits of every proceeding covered by the later settlement announcement.

observations.observation: The settlement release’s own safe-harbor section described risks around anticipated benefits, collection of previously awarded damages, appeals, and other litigation, including Netlist matters involving Google and other parties.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are issuer risk disclosures, not evidence of payment default or that the announced license and settlement would fail.
